name: Nginx Proxy Manager
author: Netlens
description: Shows the sites your Nginx Proxy Manager publishes (proxy hosts, redirections, streams, 404 hosts) and ties each one to the device or Docker container behind it: a 'Published through Nginx Proxy Manager' card on that device, the sites a proxy serves, certificate expiry with warnings, optional HTTPS checks per site and optional DNS names for the domains. Read-only: it only reads from the Nginx Proxy Manager API, so give it a user that can only view.

info.title: How to create the Nginx Proxy Manager user for Netlens
info.text: In Nginx Proxy Manager open Users and add a user for Netlens. Give it a normal e-mail address and a password, do NOT make it an administrator and do not turn on two-factor authentication for it (the API login cannot answer a code). Then open that user's Permissions and set Item Visibility to 'All Items' (otherwise it sees only what it created itself) and every permission to 'View Only'. Enter that e-mail address and password below. Netlens only ever reads.
info.code:
Users > Add User
  Email:       netlens@example.com
  Roles:       (none, not Administrator)

Users > Netlens > Permissions
  Item Visibility:    All Items
  Proxy Hosts:        View Only
  Redirection Hosts:  View Only
  404 Hosts:          View Only
  Streams:            View Only
  Access Lists:       View Only
  Certificates:       View Only

config.label: Nginx Proxy Manager
config.help: The address of the admin interface (port 81 by default) and the e-mail address and password of the read-only user. When Netlens reaches the proxy under a name or as 127.0.0.1, fill in the proxy's own network address as well, so its sites can be linked to the right device.

columns.label: Proxy's own address
columns.help: Only needed when the address above is a name or 127.0.0.1

config.label: Look up the names sites forward to
config.help: A site that forwards to a host name (nas.home.example.com) is tied to the device with that address.

config.label: Check every site
config.help: Netlens asks the proxy for each enabled site over HTTPS (or HTTP) every few minutes and reports it under Services, with a 'service down' event when the proxy answers with a server error. These checks follow the proxy's list: they come and go with the sites.

config.label: Warn about certificates this many days before they expire
config.help: You get a 'certificate expiring' event at this many days, and again at 7, 3 and 1 days and when it has expired.
